pty-integration-linux:
    # THE PR PTY/CLI integration leg (gh-1005: the former mac leg merged in;
    # before that, issue #931 part 2 sharded ONE ~40-min job into 3
    # duration-balanced shards — scripts/test_integration_shards.json,
    # file-level units). New integration-tagged files bin-pack in at runtime
    # (shard_files.py --tags integration), so a PR adding one never
    # silently skips it. Explicit --concurrency=4 bounds in-suite
    # parallelism (part 3.3 — package:test forbids `concurrency` in
    # dart_test.yaml tag overrides, so the knob lives here; it bounds
    # concurrent live-provider tests PER JOB — the rate-limit rationale is
    # documented on the llm tag in dart_test.yaml).
    # Per-shard coverage artifacts merge in pty-coverage-gate —
    # a single shard's ratchet would see partial lib/src/cli coverage
    # and false-regress. Each shard also emits the dart json
    # file-reporter: junit feeds rebalancing/budget-tightening PRs, the
    # raw json feeds the #928 duration gate (pty-coverage-gate below).
    # gh-1300: needs the once-per-run AOT build; FA_BIN points every CLI
    # spawn (PTY harness + headless helpers) at the prebuilt binary.
    needs: [release-pending, release-dedupe, fa-aot-build]
    # gh-1551: an empty schedule tick (no commits since the last v* tag)
    # skips this leg — the release-pending pre-check decides.
    if: needs.release-pending.outputs.pending == 'true' && needs.release-dedupe.outputs.dedupe != 'true'
    name: PTY/CLI integration (linux, shard ${{ matrix.shard }}/3)
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04-arm
    # 40 > 30: the leg now carries the coverage + file-reporter overhead the
    # old mac leg had (the coverage-free linux twin never paid it) and arm64
    # Graviton cores run somewhat slower than the M-series minis did — margin
    # without stretching the watchdog much.
    timeout-minutes: 40
    permissions:
      contents: read
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        shard: [0, 1, 2]
    env:
      # Secret shape (review 2026-09-23): this is the pull_request-time leg
      # that receives real provider secrets. GitHub withholds secrets from
      # forks, so external contributions never see them — but every
      # SAME-REPO branch runs this suite with the keys in its process
      # environment before human review (this repo's agent-authored-branch
      # model). The marginal escalation vs the nightly (same suites, same
      # keys, post-merge on main) is small and the watchdog already hands
      # RELEASE_PAT to same-repo PRs; documented here so the assumption is
      # explicit, not implicit.
      #
      # The live-provider legs (unlocked by these keys) load extra
      # lib/src/cli surface into the coverage measurement, so a no-key run
      # measures a DIFFERENT — lower-numbered — value; missing keys (forks)
      # self-skip those legs gracefully and the gate stays honest either
      # way.
      OPENROUTER_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.OPENROUTER_API_KEY }}
      ANTHROPIC_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.ANTHROPIC_API_KEY }}
      GOOGLE_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.GOOGLE_API_KEY }}
      OLLAMA_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.OLLAMA_API_KEY }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
      - uses: dart-lang/setup-dart@6afc89df92d6eb3834022f73cd65adc8cdfcb92d # v1
        with:
          sdk: stable
      - run: dart pub get

      - name: Native-assets hook cache
        uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        with:
          path: .dart_tool/hooks_runner/shared
          key: hooks-shared-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-${{ hashFiles('pubspec.lock') }}
          restore-keys: hooks-shared-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-

      # gh-1300: the AOT binary built once per run by fa-aot-build. The
      # guard FAILS the shard loudly if the artifact is missing or dead —
      # a silent JIT fallback would hide the optimization from AC1's
      # before/after numbers.
      - uses: ./.github/actions/sqlite3-native-assets-prewarm
      - uses: actions/download-artifact@9000827ccba6bdab643e8b6fd33ac0654aef8333 # v8.0.2
        with:
          name: fa-aot-bin
          path: fa-local/bundle
      # Artifact zips do NOT preserve the exec bit (download-artifact
      # README: "post-download the file is no longer guaranteed to be set
      # as an executable"). Run 37446280743: `test -x` below failed
      # silently ~20 ms in on EVERY shard — the gate went red before a
      # single test ran. Restore the mode the build job shipped; the
      # smoke below still verifies the restored binary is executable and
      # boots (never a silent JIT fallback). Content integrity is not
      # affected: download-artifact digest-validates (digest-mismatch:
      # error default), so this chmod only ever touches the verified
      # bundle the fa-aot-build job produced.
      - name: Restore exec bit (artifact zips drop permissions)
        run: chmod +x fa-local/bundle/bin/fa
      - name: Smoke the AOT binary (fail loud, never JIT-fallback)
        run: |
          test -x fa-local/bundle/bin/fa
          ./fa-local/bundle/bin/fa --version
      - name: dart test --tags integration (linux, shard ${{ matrix.shard }}/3)
        env:
          # gh-1300 FA_BIN seam: every CLI spawn (pty_harness + the
          # headless helpers via faCliCommand) runs the AOT binary —
          # ~1 s per spawn instead of the JIT VM+CFE compile (~30 s on
          # loaded ARM runners). Per-test isolation is unchanged.
          FA_BIN: ${{ github.workspace }}/fa-local/bundle/bin/fa
          # Issue #1391: stretch every PTY-harness wait budget 2x on this
          # merge-blocking leg. SM dispatch waves pack the hosted-arm pool
          # (refresh waves supersede PR heads mid-run), and drilled reds
          # are all single tests popping quiet-runner budgets inside
          # otherwise-green 60-70-test shards. Local runs and the nightly
          # leave the var unset and keep the exact legacy budgets (the
          # nightly's unsupervised verdicts feed quarantine decisions).
          FA_PTY_BUDGET_SCALE: '2'
        run: |
          # gh-1199 AC1: --exclude-tag llm keeps every live-provider file
          # out of the merge-blocking selection (manifest unit AND runtime
          # bin-pack); --exclude-tags browser-ext,llm is the dart-test
          # backstop. AC6: the quarantine filter drops flake-quarantined
          # files (scripts/test_quarantine.json) pending their fix PRs.
          targets=$(python3 scripts/shard_files.py scripts/test_integration_shards.json ${{ matrix.shard }} --tags integration --exclude browser_ext --exclude-tag llm | python3 scripts/apply_quarantine.py)
          echo "shard targets: $targets"
          if [ -z "$targets" ]; then
            echo "shard fully quarantined — nothing to run"
            exit 0
          fi
          mkdir -p build/test-results
          dart test --tags integration --exclude-tags browser-ext,llm \
            --concurrency=4 \
            --coverage=coverage \
            --file-reporter="json:build/test-results/integration-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.json" \
            $targets
      # The file-reporter writes the json even on a RED leg — convert +
      # upload must not be chained into the failing step (#928 review):
      # timing evidence is exactly what red runs need to keep.
      - name: junit durations (shard ${{ matrix.shard }})
        if: always()
        run: >-
          python3 scripts/junit_from_dart_json.py
          build/test-results/integration-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.json
          build/test-results/junit-integration-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.xml

commit a79212bc905ddf0eb6d55490086093a7494132e2
Author: Uladzimir Klyshevich <istin2007@gmail.com>
Date:   Sun Nov 15 19:56:22 2026 +0300

    Devices UX follow-up: phone dock, folder-grouped roster, DM presence UX, Apps header (#2196)
    
    * feat(app): Devices UX — dock Devices slot + lower gap, folder-grouped subagent-free roster, composer inset
    
    Owner feedback round:
    - Phone dock: Devices takes Activity's primary slot (Activity moves to
      More; guests keep Activity, Devices is JWT-gated) and rides 20% closer
      to the bottom edge (bottomGap 8→6.4, minInflatedBottom 62.4).
    - Subagent transcripts are never published as remote DM targets (source
      filter via isSubagentSession + visible-ids/metadata projections).
    - Remote sessions collapse into per-project-folder groups when more than
      one folder exists (Local-panel logic): collapsed by default, open DM
      session auto-expands, groups sorted by latest activity.
    - Composer: with no attach control and no leadingBuilder the bare field
      gets a 12pt leading inset instead of the 2pt icon-hugging one.
    - New FaSemanticIcon constants (folder/download/apps) keep the material
      ratchet green; narrow/wide shell goldens regenerated.
    
    * feat(app): DM conversation — fa/session sender label + agent working banner
    
    Owner feedback on Devices DMs:
    - Incoming agent replies no longer render under the owner's account
      name: the sender label is the tapped session's human title, else 'fa'
      (default app agent) or the agent name.
    - The conversation shows 'Fa is working…' while the Devices roster marks
      the peer agent busy (DeviceConnectorService.agentRunState over current
      roster frames, live updates on roster/presence) — the visible
      acknowledgement that the agent picked the message up.
    - Network-channel goldens regenerated (12pt bare-composer inset).
    
    * feat(app): phone Apps — search + Widget Catalog as header icons
    
    Owner feedback: the narrow Apps chrome (search row + My Apps/Catalog
    text tabs) left a tiny scroll area. On compact widths the search reveal
    and a catalog toggle now live in the floating page header (the messages
    header layout), the narrow tab row is gone, and a floating catalog icon
    is reserved inside the My Apps list (clears the shell's floating dock
    even when the nested navigator zeroes the ambient bottom padding).
    Wider narrow hosts keep the inline search field; desktop chrome is
    unchanged. Launcher/store goldens and fastlane screenshots regenerated.
    
    * test(app): regenerate remaining floating-dock goldens (bottomGap 6.4)
    
    * test(app): regenerate store story screenshots (Apps header chrome)
    
    * fix(app): CRAP 12 ratchet — decompose agentRunState, DM banner _refresh, Apps grid
    
    CI app-crap-gate on PR #2196 measured: DeviceConnectorService.agentRunState
    CC13@100% (13.0), _DmAgentStatusBannerState._refresh CC5@0% (30.0),
    _AppLauncherScreenState._buildGridArea CC13@98% (13.0015) — all over the
    12.0 threshold. Split the roster payload walk into three small pure
    helpers, move the banner's guard/transition logic into the unit-tested
    top-level dmRefreshedAgentRunState (_refresh is now a two-branch setter),
    and extract the narrow Apps body + inline-search visibility condition.
    No behaviour change; existing agentRunState/launcher suites + two new
    banner-transition tests green.

OK, so the PTY harness has wait budgets (10-90s, scaled ×2 in CI). A single test popping its budget yields a TimeoutException — a clean FAILURE, not a 39-minute hang. So the 39-minute total silence means something ELSE froze: either the whole runner VM was starved/frozen, or dart test itself deadlocked, or... all three in-flight tests hit awaits that have NO budget coverage (e.g. awaiting child process exit, or a stream done event).

Now let me look at the three hung tests and their final phases:

3. `test/integration/ssh_shift_gate_test.dart` — "SSH session env: the first Enter submits and Ctrl+C quits"

Let me read them, focusing on what happens at the END of each test (the phase where they'd be when frozen).

But hold on — is it possible that dart test wasn't hung at all, but rather each of these tests was legitimately LONG (e.g. the countdown test waits for 10 jobs × N seconds) and the budgets stretched ×2... no — 39 minutes vs budgets of tens of seconds is not budget stretch.

Alternative theory: the tests themselves were FINE, but the RUNER froze (degraded hosted runner — known phenomenon per "Watchdog (degraded-runner retrigger)" job). When a hosted runner disk/CPU wedges, ALL in-flight work freezes simultaneously — exactly the observed signature: 3 concurrent suites, all silent, no more log output AT ALL (not even dart's 30s-per-test timeout warnings — wait, does dart test print anything on its own? dart test only prints at the end).

Hmm — actually here's a discriminating fact: with `--concurrency=4`, four suites run at once. We have exactly 3 tests in flight in 3 suites. What about the 4th suite in the last wave? 25 targets, concurrency=4 → wave structure: suites are loaded lazily one at a time; as each finishes, the next loads. The "still loading" list was EMPTY — all 25 suites were loaded... wait no, suiteLoadStart/Done is about COMPILATION/loading. All 25 loaded. Hmm, but only 14 files had passing tests. Actually dart test concurrency bounds concurrent TESTS (isolates), and with `--concurrency=4`... for suite-level: test packages load one suite per concurrency slot, run its tests (a suite's tests run sequentially inside its isolate unless the suite defines concurrency), then the slot takes the next suite. So 25 suites over 4 slots.

The frozen state: slots were running tui_protype_snapshot (suite 13 in list order?), shell_job_countdown, ssh_shift_gate, and one more... but only 3 tests were mid-flight. The 4th slot — maybe between suites (suite finished, next loading) — or a suite whose tests had all completed but suite "done" wasn't emitted...

The order in the targets list: shell_job_countdown_pty_test, ssh_shift_gate_test, yolo_rm_critical_e2e_test, fa_cli_integration_test, trajectory/cli_integration_test, trajectory/perf_open_gate_test, fa_cli_thinking_abort_test, fa_cli_thinking_livestream_pty_test, message_cap_heal_e2e_test, pty_resume_transcript_pin_test, skills_freshness_pty_test, wire_serve_cli_test — these 12 never emitted a pass. tui_protype_snapshot DID emit (12.12s "starts with banner and input prompt") — but ANOTHER of its tests ("typing text and pressing Enter submits to viewport") was still running. So tui_protype_snapshot was mid-suite (test 2 of its suite).

So at freeze: 3 slots running tui_protype_snapshot(2nd test), shell_job_countdown, ssh_shift_gate; 4th slot had just finished something and... the next suite never started loading. 

EVERYTHING froze at once. Consistent with runner-level stall (degraded runner) OR dart test VM deadlock OR all three PTY harness spawns deadlocked the same way.

Given repo history (#1391, branch 1026-flaky-pty...), runner-level starvation on hosted arm is a known disease. But 39 minutes of TOTAL silence including no further suite loads — a starved CPU runner would still make slow progress, not zero. A frozen runner makes zero progress.

set -euo pipefail
          # The jobs endpoint intermittently answers 502 (live on the
          # gh-1086 rework head 81ed7186: a single 502 failed the whole
          # telemetry leg). Same 3-attempt pattern as build-mobile's
          # "Install Flutter dependencies" — transient API errors retry,
          # a real failure still reds the step loudly.
          for attempt in 1 2 3; do
            if gh api "repos/$REPO/actions/runs/$RUN_ID/jobs?per_page=100" > /tmp/jobs.json; then
              break
            fi
            if [ "$attempt" = 3 ]; then
              echo "::error::gh api jobs fetch failed after 3 attempts — GitHub API is erroring (502-class)"
              exit 1
            fi
            echo "::warning::gh api jobs fetch failed (attempt $attempt/3) — retrying in 10s"
            sleep 10
          done
          python3 - <<'EOF' >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
          import datetime, json
          jobs = json.load(open('/tmp/jobs.json'))['jobs']
          print('## Per-step durations\n')
          print('| job | step | duration | conclusion |')
          print('|---|---|---|---|')
          for j in jobs:
              for s in j.get('steps', []):
                  if not (s.get('started_at') and s.get('completed_at')):
                      continue
                  t0 = datetime.datetime.fromisoformat(s['started_at'].replace('Z', '+00:00'))
                  t1 = datetime.datetime.fromisoformat(s['completed_at'].replace('Z', '+00:00'))
                  print(f"| {j['name']} | {s['name']} | {int((t1 - t0).total_seconds())}s | {s['conclusion']} |")
          EOF
          cp /tmp/jobs.json step-timings.json

      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@cf430e030ddbb5b0abf93d22962f4752f3646cd9 # v7.0.2
        with:
          name: step-timings
          path: step-timings.json
          retention-days: 14

  # Issue #194 (point 4): >2x-baseline watchdog. The timeout-minutes above
  # are ≈2x the healthy job durations observed on main (shards 3-5 min,
  # flutter-tests ~6 min + fa_ui shards ~5 min since issue #283). A timeout means this run landed on a degraded
  # runner allocation; the remedy is a fresh EMPTY-COMMIT push — a new run
  # gets a fresh allocation and the push cancels this stale run via the PR
  # concurrency group. NEVER `gh run rerun`: it reallocates into the same
  # degraded pool. One retrigger max per head commit (loop guard below).
  watchdog:
    name: Watchdog (degraded-runner retrigger)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 5
    # pty-integration-linux/pty-visual ride along (review 2026-09-23, #963;
    # gh-1005 retired the mac shards): the longest legs. They must be in
    # `needs` or the watchdog fires before they settle — a degraded-runner
    # timeout there would land after the scan and never get its one-shot
    # empty-commit retrigger. Cost: the watchdog waits for them.
    needs: [changes, static, test-core, coverage-gate, guards, flutter-tests, test-faui, pty-integration-linux, pty-visual]
    # Same-repo PRs only: the empty-commit retrigger pushes to the PR branch,
    # which this token cannot do for a fork's ref.
    if: always() && github.event_name == 'pull_request' && github.event.pull_request.head.repo.full_name == github.repository
    permissions:
      actions: read
      contents: write
    steps:
      - name: Detect a timeout-type failure
        id: trip
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          REPO: ${{ github.repository }}
          RUN_ID: ${{ github.run_id }}
        run: |
          trip=false
          for id in $(gh api "repos/$REPO/actions/runs/$RUN_ID/jobs?per_page=100" \
              --jq '.jobs[] | select(.conclusion=="failure") | .id'); do
            # A job-level timeout cancels the running step: the job is
            # 'failure' but its LAST step is 'cancelled'. A real test
            # failure ends with a failed step.
            last=$(gh api "repos/$REPO/actions/jobs/$id" --jq '.steps[-1].conclusion // ""')
            echo "job $id last step: $last"
            if [ "$last" = "cancelled" ]; then trip=true; fi
          done
          echo "trip=$trip" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        if: steps.trip.outputs.trip == 'true'
        with:
          ref: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}
          # GITHUB_TOKEN pushes never trigger workflows — the retrigger must
          # re-fire CI, so it rides RELEASE_PAT (same as release/gardener).
          token: ${{ secrets.RELEASE_PAT }}

      - name: Retrigger with an empty commit (fresh runner allocation)
        if: steps.trip.outputs.trip == 'true'
        env:
          HAS_PAT: ${{ secrets.RELEASE_PAT != '' }}
        run: |
          if [ "$HAS_PAT" != "true" ]; then
            echo "::notice::RELEASE_PAT not configured — cannot retrigger"
            exit 0
          fi
          msg="ci: watchdog retrigger (degraded runner pool)"
          if [ "$(git log -1 --format=%s)" = "$msg" ]; then
            echo "head commit is already a watchdog retrigger — not looping"
            exit 0
          fi
          git config user.name "github-actions[bot]"
          git config user.email "41898282+github-actions[bot]@users.noreply.github.com"
          git commit --allow-empty -m "$msg"
          git push origin HEAD:"${{ github.event.pull_request.head.ref }}"
  integration:
    name: Provider smoke (LLM, tag-only)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: quality-gate
    timeout-minutes: 20
    permissions:
      contents: read
    # Same !cancelled() pattern as the release/binaries jobs (fa#456).
    # #1368: the gate check reads the dart_ok OUTPUT, not the aggregate
    # result — a platform-only red (Windows build, PTY leg) used to skip this
    # smoke transitively and with it the publish job (the v1.0.519-521
    # starvation). dart_ok=false (a red package leg) still skips it: the
    # publish it gates cannot run anyway.

The watchdog only fires on **pull_request** events — the v1.0.731 run was a **push (tag)** event, so the watchdog was correctly skipped and no degraded-runner retrigger happened for it.

Now let me consolidate my understanding of the failure and check remaining details:

1. Both reds (18:25 schedule run and 19:31 tag run) are on **PTY/CLI integration (linux, shard 2/3)** on the same SHA, on hosted `ubuntu-24.04-arm` runners.
2. 18:25: `jsr_cli_test.dart` suite LOAD failure ("Connection closed before full header was received" — dart test's internal browserless VM service WS handshake died). 97 passed/1 failed in ~2 min.
3. 19:31: 98 tests done in ~30 s, then the dart test process froze silently for 39 min with 3 tests mid-flight (all PTY-spawning suites) until the 40-min job timeout cancelled it.

Both are classic **degraded-runner / hosted-arm-pool starvation** signatures, NOT code regressions:
- PR #2196 touched only flutter_app/fa_ui/store/yoclip — zero fa-CLI surface.
- Same tests pass on v1.0.730's run in ~2 min/shard.
- The repo has documented history: issue #1391 (FA_PTY_BUDGET_SCALE was introduced for exactly this), the watchdog (PR-only), the flake branch 1026-flaky-pty-timing-flakes-...

Now, what is the RIGHT fix for this bug ticket? The ticket says "Closes manually when the ref goes green." So the goal: make the ref green again. Options:

A. Pure infra/retry: retrigger the tag's CI run (`gh run rerun 43752856871 --failed`). But note the watchdog comment: "NEVER `gh run rerun`: it reallocates into the same degraded pool" — that's for PR runs; for tag runs, a rerun gets a fresh allocation attempt but the docs say rerun reallocates into the same degraded pool. Also my role is "Senior Development Engineer specializing in root cause analysis and bug fixing" — I should fix the ROOT CAUSE in the repo if possible, then the post-processing commits/PRs it.

B. Fix a product/test bug. Is there one? Candidate real bugs found:
  1. **Shard 2/3 is systematically the red one.** Two consecutive failures on the same shard. Why shard 2? The shard bin-packing: shard_files.py balances file counts/durations. Shard 2 got 25 targets including the heaviest PTY tests? Shards 0 and 1 passed in ~2-3 min. Shard 2 has 25 files — MORE than 1/3. Hmm wait, actually the target list for shard 2 had 25 files. Let me check shard 0 and 1 target counts. If shard 2 carries substantially more suites than the others, it's the biggest timeout risk. The junit said 80 tests for shard 2... but the schedule run said "97 tests passed, 1 failed" — 98 tests. Hmm, in the tag run only 80 testcases in junit — because 18 tests (in the 12 never-started files + 3 hung) never completed. 80 + 18 = 98. OK.

  Let me check the shard sizes: test_integration_shards.json + shard_files.py balance. 25 files in shard 2 — let me count shard 0/1's targets from their logs.

  2. **The freeze has no in-process bound**: when dart test wedges, NOTHING bounds it except the 40-min job timeout. The repo could add a per-run wall-clock guard (e.g. `timeout 15m dart test ...` or dart_test.yaml `timeout`) so a wedge fails FAST with diagnostics instead of burning 40 min and producing "cancelled" (which also dodges the junit/quarantine evidence — the run produced a cancelled run conclusion, which per "Red-in-≥2-distinct-SHA-runs flakes quarantine" may not even register in flake stats).

  3. The **watchdog is PR-only** — tag/main runs with the same degraded-runner signature get no retrigger. Extending the watchdog to tag pushes (empty commit can't happen on a tag though — the retrigger pushes to the PR branch; for tags there's nothing to push). Hmm.

Given my role — "bug fixing" agent with TDD — I need to decide: is there a product-code fix warranted here, or is the right move an RCA + a guard?

Let me dig one more level: WHY did dart test freeze? Is there a KNOWN hang bug in these tests? Let me check the 3 hung tests' last phase again:

- tui_protype_snapshot_test.dart: "typing text and pressing Enter submits to viewport" — @Timeout(2 min). t=20316ms started. 2-min timeout would fire at ~t+140s. Nothing. So the test ISOLATE event loop was dead — timers don't fire when the isolate is stuck. All three isolates dead at once = the dart TEST process (they share one process) frozen. When the main dart test process freezes (event loop of the coordinator... actually each suite runs in its own isolate, but they're all in the same OS process). A process-level freeze (e.g. blocked in a syscall — fork bomb/memory exhaustion) explains all timers dead simultaneously.

Wait, actually — one more possibility I should rule out: dart test's coverage handler. `--coverage=coverage` makes the VM write coverage per isolate on isolate exit. There are known Dart VM issues where coverage collection hangs when many isolates... And the orphan processes: "Terminate orphan process: pid (2412) (dart:concatenat)" + "pid (2476) (dart:dartdev_ao)" — dart:concatenate = kernel concatenation service, dartdev_ao = dartdev AOT helper. These are the **dart test frontend's own** helper processes? Actually "dartdev_ao" is likely "dartdev_aot" — the AOT snapshot of dartdev used by `dart test`... hmm, `dart test` runs the frontend server + kernel service (concatenat). Those orphans existed at cleanup — the test run's dill/kernel service. Their presence at cleanup is normal-ish for a killed run.

I can't root-cause the freeze below "process froze" from the evidence. But the scheduled-run red gives a much more tractable root cause candidate: `Connection closed before full header was received` — this is the load failure of the SAME shard. Let me look for known GitHub issues in this repo about it.

# Root Cause Analysis — gh-2200 `[ci-red] v1.0.731 failed`

## Root Cause Analysis

**Bug**: Tag-train CI run 43752856871 (v1.0.731, SHA `a79212b`) went red —
`PTY/CLI integration (linux, shard 2/3)` was cancelled at its 40-minute job
timeout, the aggregate **Quality gate** then failed (`cancelled` ≠
`success`), the skipped `release-provenance` left v1.0.731 an unsigned
draft, and the `if: always()` `Advance vpinned marker` job correctly
refused to move the marker
(`E_PIN_PROVENANCE_MISSING`, no `SHA256SUMS` on the draft release).

**Root cause**: Degraded hosted `ubuntu-24.04-arm` runner during the SM
dispatch wave — the known hostile-ambient class (issues #965, #1391;
precedent #2124) — **not a product defect**. Evidence:

1. **No code surface changed.** PR #2196 (`a79212b`) touches 86 files —
   83 `flutter_app/**` + 3 `packages/fa_ui/**` (chat composer icon
   constants + ergonomics test). `lib/`, `bin/` and root `test/` — the
   only code compiled into the fa AOT binary the PTY suites drive — are
   untouched.
2. **Two independent reds, same SHA, same shard 2/3, different failure
   modes** — the signature of a sick runner allocation, not a code bug:
   - Run 43746679560 (schedule, 18:25Z): suite-load death — `Failed to
     load "test/cli/jsr_cli_test.dart": Connection closed before full
     header was received` (package:test WS handshake lost), 97 passed /
     1 failed in ~2 min. Byte-identical to the one-shot loader flake
     resolved as transient in #2124 (v1.0.710).
   - Run 43752856871 (tag, 19:31Z): 98 tests completed in ~30 s, then the
     `dart test` process froze with **zero output for 39 minutes** with 3
     suites mid-flight (`tui_prototype_snapshot` 2-min, `ssh_shift_gate`
     5-min, `shell_job_countdown_pty` 8-min `@Timeout` — none fired ⇒
     whole-process stall, timers dead) until the 40-min `timeout-minutes`
     cancelled the job. Two orphan dart helper processes were reaped at
     cleanup.
3. **Baseline**: the same shards on v1.0.730's run 43737206213 completed
   in ~2–3 min each, all green.
4. **The repo's own playbook matches**: `lib/src/cli/pty_wait_budget.dart`
   (#1391) — "SM dispatch waves pack the hosted-arm pool … a single test
   pops its budget inside an otherwise-green shard". The
   `watchdog:` job (ci.yml, degraded-runner retrigger) exists for exactly
   this but is `pull_request`-only — tag trains get no auto-retrigger.

**Impact**: The v1.0.731 release train stalled mid-run: aggregate gate
red, `SHA256SUMS` unsigned, draft unpublished, `vpinned` marker stale at
v1.0.730. Pinned-install consumers keep resolving v1.0.730. No product or
user-facing code is affected.

**Fix approach**: No product-code change — the red is the documented
release-flow failure class: per `docs/agents/quality-gates.md` "a red tag
run is a release-flow failure, triaged by daily-publish / ci-red-report,
never quarantined as a flake" (quarantine needs ≥2 distinct-SHA reds;
both reds here are the same SHA). Remedy = tag-train recovery: re-run the
failed jobs of run 43752856871 on a fresh allocation
(`gh run rerun --failed`; an empty-commit retrigger is impossible for an
immutable tag), letting shard 2/3 → Quality gate → release-provenance →
publish → install-pin-bump complete, i.e. the ref goes green and the
marker advances. Verified locally before rerun: the identical shard-2
target list passes on this commit.

# gh-1832: the REQUIRED release-asset set — the single source of truth.
#
# Consumers (all read this one file, never a private copy):
#   - ci.yml release-provenance "Assert required release assets" step —
#     the publish-blocking gate: runs scripts/assert_release_assets.sh
#     <tag> BEFORE the signed-checksums upload and the --draft=false
#     --latest flip. A missing asset leaves the release a DRAFT (the
#     previous release stays latest) and fails the release run loudly.
#   - ci.yml release-asset-smoke job — post-publish: --smoke ranged-GETs
#     every asset here (red on non-200/206) and --landing probes every
#     releases/(latest/)?download/ URL the fa1.dev landing page exposes.
#
# Scope: exactly the fa-* set a usable release must serve (v1.0.634 is the
# reference shape — v1.0.635 shipped without fa-extension.zip, gh-1832):
# `fa update` channels (linux/macos/windows archives), the web SPA and the
# Chrome extension the landing page links directly.
#
# Producers (gh-1847): fa-extension.zip is built by the TAG TRAIN itself
# (ci.yml build-extension, additive leg) since the once-daily build-macos
# producer kept stranding tag trains that landed after the daily leg
# (v1.0.637/v1.0.638, 2026-10-24); the daily build-macos leg survives as
# the next-tag-draft pre-stager and the n_1012 emergency producer.
#
# Deliberately NOT here: SHA256SUMS(.sig) — release-provenance itself
# produces them after this gate runs; DMGs/zips/latest-mac.yml and the
# store artifacts (apk/aab/ipa) — they come from the separately-dispatched
# daily mobile/macOS legs (a flaky self-hosted runner must never hold the
# CLI/web/extension train hostage) and are clobber-refresher assets, not
# publish blockers.
#
# One literal asset name per line; '#' starts a comment. The gate matches
# exact names — no globs.
fa-extension.zip
fa-linux-arm64.tar.gz
fa-linux-x64.tar.gz
fa-macos-arm64.tar.gz
fa-macos-x64.tar.gz
fa-web-spa.zip
fa-windows-x64.zip

# Coverage home for the SHARDED pty-integration-linux leg (mirrors
  # faui-coverage): the 3 shard lcovs merge into ONE report (union DA hits
  # per file, NOT cat — a single shard's ratchet would see partial
  # lib/src/cli coverage and false-regress), then the CLI coverage ratchet
  # runs on the merged report, and the duration-budget gate (issue #928
  # Part 1) consumes the leg's three dart-json shard reports:
  # per-suite totals vs scripts/test_duration_baseline.json (down-only
  # ratchet, >10% suite regression or a per-test budget breach fails the
  # merge) and the top-10 slowest tests land in the job summary on every
  # run. The gate NEVER rewrites the baseline — budgets move only through
  # reviewed PRs running check_test_durations.py --update-baseline locally
  # against an integration-json artifact. gh-1005: the measurement
  # environment moved mac -> ubuntu-24.04-arm together with the leg (the
  # coverage-gardener already measured on ubuntu); a baseline re-seat, if
  # the first linux runs sit below the floor, takes the same reviewed-PR
  # path.
  pty-coverage-gate:
    name: PTY gates (coverage ratchet + duration budget, merged shards)
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04-arm
    needs: [release-pending, release-dedupe, pty-integration-linux]
    # gh-1551: an empty schedule tick (no commits since the last v* tag)
    # skips this leg — the release-pending pre-check decides.
    if: needs.release-pending.outputs.pending == 'true' && needs.release-dedupe.outputs.dedupe != 'true'
    timeout-minutes: 5
    permissions:
      contents: read
      # gh-1300: issues: write — the duration-budget auto-filer files/
      # comments/closes the [ENH] optimization issue. A job-level
      # permissions block drops every unlisted scope to none, so both
      # scopes are listed explicitly (the filing leg reads nothing else).
      issues: write
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
      - uses: actions/setup-python@6d4fd22b20465ccc0f7354476588e8df7c9ca0e0 # v7.1.0
        with:
          python-version: '3.x'
      - uses: actions/download-artifact@9000827ccba6bdab643e8b6fd33ac0654aef8333 # v8.0.2
        with:
          pattern: pty-coverage-shard-*
          path: pty-coverage-shards
      # Same discipline as the core/faui shards' assert_shard_manifest: the 3
      # selections must cover exactly the integration-tagged suite
      # (browser-ext excluded, it owns browser-ext.yml), pairwise disjoint,
      # every unit on disk. Fails loudly BEFORE the ratchet reads shard data.
      - name: Assert integration shard manifest (union/disjoint/exists)
        run: python3 scripts/assert_shard_manifest.py scripts/test_integration_shards.json --shards 3 --tags integration --exclude browser_ext --exclude-tag llm
      # The leg's dart json reports for the #928 duration gate below.
      - uses: actions/download-artifact@9000827ccba6bdab643e8b6fd33ac0654aef8333 # v8.0.2
        with:
          pattern: integration-json-shard-*
          path: integration-json-shards
      - name: Merge shard coverage (union DA hits per file, NOT cat)
        run: |
          count=$(ls pty-coverage-shards/*/lcov.info | wc -l | tr -d ' ')
          if [ "$count" != "3" ]; then
            echo "::error::expected 3 pty shard coverage reports, got $count"
            exit 1
          fi
          # gh-995: a report that downloads but carries no SF: records
          # (empty/truncated upload) still satisfies the count check and
          # merges into a silently partial report — the 2026-09-27 wedge
          # also showed the ratchet reading 7.95% vs the 11.00% baseline
          # off exactly such a merge. Fail loudly naming the hollow shard
          # instead of letting the ratchet chase a phantom regression.
          for f in pty-coverage-shards/*/lcov.info; do
            grep -q '^SF:' "$f" || { echo "::error::$f carries no SF: records — hollow shard coverage upload"; exit 1; }
          done
          mkdir -p coverage
          python3 scripts/merge_lcov.py \
            -o coverage/lcov.merged.info \
            pty-coverage-shards/*/lcov.info
      - name: CLI coverage ratchet (lib/src/cli/**, baseline only up)
        run: python3 scripts/check_cli_coverage.py --lcov coverage/lcov.merged.info
      - name: Test duration budget gate (issue #928, ratchet only down)
        run: |
          ls integration-json-shards/*
          python3 scripts/check_test_durations.py \
            --baseline scripts/test_duration_baseline.json \
            integration-json-shards/*/integration-shard-*.json
      # gh-1300: per-SHARD budget (expected runner span + headroom, one
      # place: scripts/test_shard_budgets.json). Breach fails the job
      # LOUDLY and writes the [ENH] issue body the filer step below posts
      # — crossing the line always produces work, never a silent bump.
      - name: Shard duration budget gate (gh-1300, down-only ratchet)
        id: shard_budget
        run: |
          python3 scripts/check_shard_durations.py \
            --budgets scripts/test_shard_budgets.json \
            --issue-body duration-budget-issue.md \
            --run-url "$GITHUB_SERVER_URL/$GITHUB_REPOSITORY/actions/runs/$GITHUB_RUN_ID" \
            integration-json-shards/*/integration-shard-*.json
      # Best-effort on forks (their GITHUB_TOKEN cannot write issues);
      # the gate failure above is the loud part. Deduped: an open
      # duration-budget issue is commented with the fresh numbers, not
      # duplicated (the nightly-red / flake-quarantine pattern).
      - name: File the duration-budget optimization issue (gh-1300)
        if: always() && steps.shard_budget.outcome == 'failure'
        continue-on-error: true
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
        run: |

# timing evidence is exactly what red runs need to keep.
      - name: junit durations (shard ${{ matrix.shard }})
        if: always()
        run: >-
          python3 scripts/junit_from_dart_json.py
          build/test-results/integration-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.json
          build/test-results/junit-integration-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.xml
      # Raw dart json for the #928 duration gate (per-test spans incl. suite
      # paths); junit is the human/rebalancer-facing form of the same data.
      # Upload MUST stay on the current upload-artifact line (gh-995): the
      # gate's download-artifact v8 digest-validates every download, so an
      # old-line upload digest-mismatches and the shard merge loses its
      # report (test/gh995_artifact_action_pins_test.dart pins the pin).
      #
      # gh-1412: each evidence upload carries a one-shot retry (the step
      # right after it, same pinned action). The gh-1412 validation run
      # 37807820733 red'd a shard whose 68 tests ALL passed on a single
      # transient `Failed to FinalizeArtifact: ECONNRESET` from GitHub's
      # blob storage — the aggregate gate followed and the merge aborted.
      # The retry re-runs the SAME action with overwrite:true (a failed
      # attempt leaves the artifact half-registered — without overwrite the
      # retry dies on "already exists"); a genuinely dead endpoint still
      # fails the shard loudly, and the retries stay if: always()-reachable
      # so red legs keep their evidence. Guarded by
      # test/ci_pty_artifact_upload_retry_guard_test.dart.
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@cf430e030ddbb5b0abf93d22962f4752f3646cd9 # v7.0.2
        id: upload_integration_json
        if: always()
        with:
          name: integration-json-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}
          path: build/test-results/integration-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.json
          retention-days: 2
      - name: Retry integration-json upload (transient blob-storage reset, gh-1412)
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@cf430e030ddbb5b0abf93d22962f4752f3646cd9 # v7.0.2
        if: always() && steps.upload_integration_json.outcome == 'failure'
        with:
          name: integration-json-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}
          path: build/test-results/integration-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.json
          retention-days: 2
          overwrite: true
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@cf430e030ddbb5b0abf93d22962f4752f3646cd9 # v7.0.2
        id: upload_integration_junit
        if: always()
        with:
          name: junit-integration-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}
          path: build/test-results/junit-integration-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.xml
          retention-days: 7
      - name: Retry junit upload (transient blob-storage reset, gh-1412)
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@cf430e030ddbb5b0abf93d22962f4752f3646cd9 # v7.0.2
        if: always() && steps.upload_integration_junit.outcome == 'failure'
        with:
          name: junit-integration-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}
          path: build/test-results/junit-integration-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.xml
          retention-days: 7
          overwrite: true
      # coverage/ is written incrementally — a red leg still formats and
      # uploads so the gate below merges what ran.
      - name: Format coverage to lcov (shard ${{ matrix.shard }})
        if: always()
        run: dart run coverage:format_coverage --lcov -i coverage -o coverage/lcov.info
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@cf430e030ddbb5b0abf93d22962f4752f3646cd9 # v7.0.2
        id: upload_pty_coverage
        if: always()
        with:
          name: pty-coverage-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}
          path: coverage/lcov.info
          retention-days: 2
      - name: Retry coverage upload (transient blob-storage reset, gh-1412)
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@cf430e030ddbb5b0abf93d22962f4752f3646cd9 # v7.0.2
        if: always() && steps.upload_pty_coverage.outcome == 'failure'
        with:
          name: pty-coverage-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}
          path: coverage/lcov.info
          retention-days: 2
          overwrite: true

arguments.newText:
**Fix approach**: Two layers.

1. **Recovery of the stalled train (no code change):** the red is the
   documented release-flow failure class — per
   `docs/agents/quality-gates.md` "a red tag run is a release-flow
   failure, triaged by daily-publish / ci-red-report, never quarantined
   as a flake" (quarantine needs ≥2 distinct-SHA reds; both reds here are
   the same SHA). Remedy = `gh run rerun --failed` on run 43752856871;
   attempt 2 re-ran shard 2/3 on a fresh allocation and it passed every
   test (also proven locally: the full shard-2 target list is green on
   `a79212b` with a clean env).

2. **Rerun-idempotency fix (code change, this branch):** attempt 2
   exposed a second-order pipeline bug. On a `rerun --failed` the
   gh-1412 retry steps never fire (the first attempt's uploads
   succeeded), so the rerun uploaded a **second same-named artifact**
   (`integration-json-shard-2` existed as IDs 14179115340 +
   14179068577) and `actions/download-artifact` pattern-mode resolved
   the **stale** one — `pty-coverage-gate` merged the truncated
   hung-run report (missing the suites the cancelled attempt never
   started) and phantom-failed with
   `budgeted suite did not run: trajectory/cli_integration_test.dart /
   trajectory/perf_open_gate_test.dart` although the rerun shard passed
   every test; the aggregate Quality gate followed (platform_red).
   Fix: the three primary evidence uploads in `pty-integration-linux`
   (`integration-json`, `junit`, `pty-coverage`) now carry
   `overwrite: true` — a rerun attempt replaces its previous attempt's
   artifact, so the merged gates always read the freshest complete
   report. Pinned by new AC4 in
   `test/ci_pty_artifact_upload_retry_guard_test.dart`.
   Operational recovery for attempt 3: the stale attempt-1 artifacts
   were deleted from the run, leaving the complete attempt-2 reports as
   the unambiguous download targets.

arguments.content:
### Root Cause

`[ci-red] v1.0.731` (run 43752856871, SHA `a79212b`) — `PTY/CLI integration (linux, shard 2/3)` froze mid-run: 98 tests passed in ~30 s, then the `dart test` process went silent for 39 min with three `@Timeout`-bounded suites in flight (none of the 2/5/8-min timeouts fired ⇒ whole-process stall) until the 40-min job timeout cancelled it. The aggregate **Quality gate** failed on the cancelled leg, the skipped `release-provenance` left v1.0.731 an unsigned draft, and `Advance vpinned marker` correctly refused to move the marker (`E_PIN_PROVENANCE_MISSING`). Same-SHA schedule run 43746679560 red'd the same shard with a different failure (`Connection closed before full header was received` loading `test/cli/jsr_cli_test.dart`) — two failure modes on one shard = degraded hosted `ubuntu-24.04-arm` runner, the hostile-ambient class of #965/#1391, not a product defect: PR #2196 touches only `flutter_app/**` + 3 `packages/fa_ui` files, nothing compiled into the fa CLI binary these suites drive. Locally the identical shard-2 target list is green on `a79212b` (122 passed; the 3 frozen suites pass; 7 sandbox-only failures were my session's ambient `FA_PROVIDERS_QUEUE` hijacking the spawned `fa` toward a live provider — CI never sets those, and a scrubbed-env rerun passes 10/10).

### Fix

Two layers:

- `gh run rerun --failed` — attempt 2 passed **every shard-2 test** on a fresh allocation, confirming the environment-only red.
- Attempt 2 exposed a rerun gap, now fixed on branch `ai/gh-2200`: `rerun --failed` never fires the gh-1412 upload retries (the first attempt's uploads succeeded), so the rerun uploaded a **second same-named artifact** and `download-artifact` pattern-mode resolved the **stale** attempt-1 report — `pty-coverage-gate` merged the truncated hung-run json and phantom-failed `budgeted suite did not run: trajectory/cli_integration_test.dart / trajectory/perf_open_gate_test.dart` although the rerun shard passed every test; the aggregate Quality gate followed. Change: the three primary evidence uploads in `pty-integration-linux` (`integration-json`, `junit`, `pty-coverage`) now carry `overwrite: true` — a rerun replaces the previous attempt's artifact, so merged gates always read the freshest complete report. Stale attempt-1 artifacts were deleted from the run for the attempt-3 recovery.

### Test Coverage

- `test/ci_pty_artifact_upload_retry_guard_test.dart` — new AC4 pins `overwrite: true` on every primary upload; full file 5/5 PASS (RED first against the old ci.yml, then GREEN after the fix).
- Local shard-2 target list on `a79212b`: 122 passed / 0 product failures (see Root Cause for the ambient-env note).
- CI attempt 3 (stale artifacts deleted): `PTY gates (coverage ratchet + duration budget)` **success**, **Quality gate success**, release chain completed — see Notes.

### Notes

- No product-code change: `lib/`, `bin/`, root `test/` are untouched by the fix commit — the branch carries the CI-workflow hardening + its guard test only.
- Same duplicate-artifact hazard exists for the core/faui shard uploads (`junit-shard-*`, `coverage-shard-*`, `faui-coverage-*`) consumed by `coverage-gate`/`faui coverage merge`; left untouched here (not this train's red) — worth the same `overwrite: true` treatment in a follow-up.
- The `watchdog` degraded-runner retrigger is `pull_request`-only, so tag trains get no auto-retrigger on runner-degradation timeouts; also worth a follow-up.
